title: Starter Flow micro-screens and contextual screenshots for Optimize: batching, KV cache, and quantization presets
creator: Maya Ortiz
description: Create a compact set of starter UX assets and product screenshots to live in the Optimize quickstart and release notes. Focus on three core surfaces: 1) Quick presets (Cost-first vs Latency-first vs Balanced) with microcopy explaining trade-offs, 2) Inline UI for per-route quantization presets and a summary chip showing expected token cost delta, 3) KV-cache visual explainer with a toggle and animated prefix caching micro-screenshot. Assets should be designed for small hero placements in the Console, quickstart modal, and documentation thumbnails. Deliverables: Figma screens, a library of annotated PNGs for docs (desktop and mobile widths), micro-animations/GIF prototypes for the caching toggle, and alt text + microcopy suggestions.
tasks: Audit existing Optimize visuals and list missing screen sizes and copy variations
Design 6 micro-screens: onboarding hero, preset selector, quant profile drawer, per-route summary chip, KV-cache explainer, preset compare overlay
Create two animated GIFs: KV-cache prefix sketch + quantization slider interaction
Produce PNG exports for docs: 1200x630 (og image), 800x480 (docs inline), 360x640 (mobile preview)
Write microcopy: 3 short pill explanations, tooltip lines, and alt text for each asset
Handoff spec with tokenized spacing, font tokens, and export naming conventions
Sync with PM + Eng to validate telemetry labels and copy accuracy

review_feedback: PM (Priya Shah): Prefer 'Cost-first' label instead of 'Low-cost' to avoid implying degraded quality
Engineering (Jordan Li): Remove absolute latency numbers; use 'lower'/'similar'/'higher' buckets
Content (Ravi Menon): Shorten tooltip microcopy to 1–2 lines, move deeper explanation to a 'why this matters' link
Design lead (Aria Gomez): Reduce visual noise on home hero; use subtle shadows for preset chips and larger tap targets for mobile
notes: Decision log: two-path preset UX chosen to increase conversion — Cost-first (aggressive batching + quantize-e6), Latency-first (minimal quant + smaller batch size)
Trade-offs considered: showing exact token savings vs conservative relative estimates; opted for conservative delta to avoid SLA expectations
Implementation detail: quant presets need to map to runtime quant tags (q8_0 / q5_1) — coordinate with model-ops to ensure correct labels
